clauses.current_legal_basis: The establishment of the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal in Section 1 continues because no end is stated and no held later instrument revokes or amends it; the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal for personnel of the Armed Forces who after July 1, 1958 meet the conditions in paragraphs (a) and (b). It states no end, none of the held later instruments (Executive Orders 11382, 13286, 11231, 13154 and 13289) revokes or amends it, and no instrument revoking the order is shown by the bounded searches, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The participation condition in Section 1(a) continues because no end is stated, no held later instrument amends it and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Paragraph (a) requires participation as members of United States military units in a United States military operation in which, in the opinion of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, personnel of any military department participate in significant numbers. It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the order is not shown revoked, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The foreign-opposition condition in Section 1(b) continues because no end is stated, no held later instrument amends it and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Paragraph (b) requires encounter of foreign armed opposition, or placement where, in the opinion of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, hostile action by foreign armed forces was imminent. It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the order is not shown revoked, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Section 2, as amended by Executive Orders 11382 and 13286, continues because the amendments only change the officer named for the Coast Guard and no instrument ends the order in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (strike Secretary of the Treasury, insert Secretary of Transportation)
amendment (strike Secretary of Transportation, insert Secretary of Homeland Security), effective March 1, 2003 under section 92

clauses.reason: Section 2 as issued in 1961 has the medal designed as approved by the Secretary of Defense and awarded by the Secretary of the military department directly concerned, and by the Secretary of the Treasury with respect to the United States Coast Guard, under uniform regulations to be issued by the Secretary of Defense. Executive Order 11382 (32 FR 16247, November 29, 1967; signed 1967-11-28), whose held text has no separate effective-date sentence, amended it by striking Secretary of the Treasury and inserting Secretary of Transportation. Executive Order 13286 section 72 (68 FR 10619, March 5, 2003), effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92, further amended section 2 by striking Secretary of Transportation and inserting Secretary of Homeland Security. Both are word substitutions only; under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, and the parent has not been revoked. Section 2 is operative on 2026-10-14 as amended.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Section 3 continues, subject to the carve-outs for Vietnam, Kosovo and global war on terrorism service in Executive Orders 11231, 13154 and 13289, because those orders do not end it and no instrument ends the order in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.

later_events.mechanism: partial carve-out notwithstanding section 3 (global war on terrorism service)

clauses.reason: Section 3 limits the medal to operations for which no other United States campaign medal is approved, requires for single-department operations that no other suitable award be available, and allows one medal per person with a device for each succeeding operation. Executive Orders 11231 (Vietnam Service Medal, section 2), 13154 (Kosovo Campaign Medal, section 2) and 13289 (Global War on Terrorism Medals, section 3) each provide notwithstanding section 3 of this order that members who qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal for service in the named theatre remain qualified and may on application receive the new medal in lieu of it. Each is a later event that carves out a defined class from Section 3's one-medal and no-other-medal limits; none revokes Section 3, which still governs all other operations. Section 3 is operative on 2026-10-14 as qualified.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The posthumous-award provision in Section 4 continues because no end is stated, no held later instrument amends it and the searches checked through 2026-10-14 show no revocation.
clauses.reason: Section 4 allows the medal to be awarded posthumously and presented to a representative of the deceased deemed appropriate by the Secretary of the department concerned. It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the order is not shown revoked, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 10977 (26 FR 11471; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10977.txt) in full: it establishes the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal (Section 1 with paragraphs (a) and (b)), has the medal designed and awarded by the Defense, military department and Coast Guard officers named in Section 2, limits awards in Section 3 and allows posthumous award in Section 4. The prepared inventory merged Sections 2, 3 and 4 into one clause, so the inventory is corrected to six clauses by characters. The held later instruments are Executive Order 11382 (32 FR 16247) and Executive Order 13286 section 72, which in turn replace the Coast Guard officer named in Section 2 (Treasury, then Transportation, then Homeland Security), and Executive Orders 11231, 13154 and 13289, which each provide 'notwithstanding section 3' that holders of the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal for service in Vietnam, Kosovo or the global war on terrorism remain qualified and may take the new medal in lieu. None revokes or supersedes the order. The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes with three hits that are the amendments above) and show no instrument ending the order. Every clause is therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route. Limits: Executive Order 13286 is cited here through the American Presidency Project capture selected by the dossier; the held Federal Register copy of its text confirms the same section 72 and the effective date in its section 92. The U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14.

savings.reason: EO 10977 has no savings or transitional provision; medals already awarded are not undone by any held later instrument, and the carve-outs in Executive Orders 11231, 13154 and 13289 expressly preserve qualification for the medal.
